access.who: any logged-in user, for their own account (also before a forced password change where allowed)

description:
The hospital's staff learn the software from the handbook the frontend team ships inside the desktop app as a
localhost-only searchable help site (guide "The end-user handbook"). This answer is its table of contents for THIS
user: the workspaces (their own first), the screens they may open (a screen of their own workspaces appears when the
server lets them call at least one of its endpoints; so does a screen of another workspace that one of theirs also
uses, `also_uses` of `GET /meta/workspaces`, listed in their workspace with `workspace` still naming its own: the
Owner's Receivables; any other screen of another workspace only when they may call every endpoint of it that needs a
permission) and, per screen, the tasks they may do in user words, the rules the page explains and
the realtime updates. The help window shows exactly these pages (`page` = `screens/<id>`, `workspaces/<code>`) and
builds its search over them, so nobody reads how to do what they are not allowed to do. Call it after login and
after a role change; the "?" button of a screen opens `screens/<its id>`.

F1 in a workspace window passes that window's `workspace`: the answer then lists that workspace and the shared screens
only, even for a user with several roles (`active_workspace`); without the parameter the window's `X-Active-Workspace`
header decides; on the launcher, call it with neither. An
unknown workspace: `VALIDATION_ERROR`; one that is not the user's: `FORBIDDEN`. The screens and workspaces of a service
that shows nothing now (`GET /establishment` views: hidden) are left out, and each screen says what it shows (`view`).

`faq_seed` lists the questions the FAQ of each listed workspace must answer, at least: one per error a screen of the
workspace can meet (the errors every screen meets, explained once by the general error help, are left out) and one
per state machine its screens move. Questions only: the help writes the answers in the user's words.

`print=true` with `workspace` adds `print_edition`: the cover (the hospital, its PHC number and category, the
workspace, the version and the date) and the chapters in print order (the workspace page, its screens, the shared
screens, the FAQ), from which the app compiles the printable guide of that workspace from the same pages as F1.
`print=true` without `workspace`: `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

The help site shows exactly these pages and searches only them.

server_time.title: Server Time
server_time.description: Server clock (UTC). Use it to detect terminal clock skew.

screens.title: Outstanding dues (Udhaar)

tasks.summary: Outstanding Patient Dues queue (with age of debt)

rules: 'Write off' (with its reason) only for finance.ar.write_off: the Owner and the Hospital Admin, who open this screen from their workspace; a cashier collects and settles but never writes off.

workspaces.label: Admissions Desk
workspaces.description: Pending admissions, live bed matrix, bed allocation, waitlists, overflow.

screens.title: Record a complaint
screens.purpose: Record a complaint as it is made, verbally or in writing, and give the complainant the tracking number.
rules: Form: how it came (in person, telephone, letter, suggestion box, from the Punjab Healthcare Commission), the complainant and how to reach them (a phone or an address unless anonymous or from the box), the patient (search by MRN) or the admission, the department, the category, the complaint in their words, what they ask for. Send an Idempotency-Key.
Give the complainant the complaint_number at once: it is their tracking number. The complaints officer acknowledges it within the day with the name of their contact person.
An appeal against the outcome comes to any desk: open the complaint (GET /complaints?mine=true or by number) and 'Record appeal' while can_appeal (COMPLAINT_APPEAL_LATE after the window).

workspaces.label: Badge station kiosk
workspaces.description: Not a user workspace: the full-screen page of a barcode-scanner badge station (no login; authenticated by the station's key).

screens.title: Badge station kiosk
screens.purpose: Full-screen page on a PC / tablet with a barcode scanner (or camera): staff show their badge, the page posts the scan and flashes the outcome. No login, no keyboard for the person scanning.

tasks.summary: Kiosk screen setup: what this station does (station-authenticated)
A badge was presented at a station (station-authenticated, no user login)

rules: Configure once with the station id and its key (X-Station-Key); never show the key.
A USB scanner types the code and Enter: keep an invisible input focused; or decode the camera stream.
needs_bed_code: collect two scans (bed sticker HMS-BED-… and badge) within 60 s, then post them together.

shared_screens.title: Report an incident
shared_screens.purpose: Anyone reports an incident, an adverse event or a near miss, the same day, without blame.

tasks.summary: What to report: the incident types
Report an incident, an adverse event or a near miss

rules: A button on every workspace's toolbar. Form: the type (GET /incident-types, grouped by area, sentinel types marked), incident or near miss, harm, when (now by default) and where (department, ward, place), who was affected (a patient: search by MRN; staff: the employee), what happened (facts, not blame) and what was done at once; 'Keep my name confidential' (reporter_confidential).
Medication errors: the stage and the medicine; theatre events: the operation and the phase (INCIDENT_DETAILS_REQUIRED). Send an Idempotency-Key: a double click must not report twice.
After sending: show the incident number and 'The Quality Officer will review it'. 'My reports' = GET /incidents?mine=true.

shared_screens.title: Incidents I investigate
shared_screens.purpose: The analysis of an incident the Quality Officer asked you to investigate, and its actions.

tasks.summary: Save the analysis (a draft until signed)

rules: List: GET /incidents?mine=true&status=UnderReview (analysis_overdue in red). Show it only to users who have one (notification category incident when named).

Analysis form (save as you go with PUT): method (RootCauseAnalysis for a sentinel event), what happened in order, root causes, contributing factors (checkboxes of the fixed list), lessons, whether the patient or the family was told and how, any report made outside (DRAP, PHC).
Sign: INCIDENT_ANALYSIS_INCOMPLETE lists details.missing. A sentinel event needs at least one factor of the system, not only 'Individual' or 'Patient' (MSDS CQI 107: blame alone is not an analysis).

shared_screens.title: Complaints I investigate
shared_screens.purpose: The complaints the complaints officer asked you to investigate: the findings, keeping the complainant informed, the actions.

tasks.summary: Write the findings of the investigation

rules: List: GET /complaints?mine=true&status=Acknowledged, by answer_due (answer_overdue in red). Show the screen only to users who have one (notification category complaint).
Findings: what the investigation found (facts, the people spoken to, the records read). The complaints officer conveys the outcome.
Tell the complainant how it stands, or that it needs more time and until when (Extension), before answer_due.

faq_seed.question: The Outstanding dues (Udhaar) screen says "Open a cash shift before handling cash." (SHIFT_NOT_OPEN). Why, and what do I do?
What do the states of a complaint mean (Received, Acknowledged, Resolved, Appealed, Closed, Withdrawn, NotMaintainable), and what moves it from one to the next?
The Record a complaint screen says "The appeal window of this complaint has ended." (COMPLAINT_APPEAL_LATE). Why, and what do I do?
